info.title: Pizza 4P's POS Console API
info.description: The `/admin` surface the back-office console is built on. Generated from the handlers; see ADR-0019. Requests, parameters and outcomes are documented; success bodies are described in prose rather than as schemas (the module docstring explains why). Every failure carries the AIP-193 `ErrorResponse` envelope.

post.summary: A super-admin issues an activation code bound to a device slot.

requestBody.description: The device slot: `tenant_id`, `store_id` and `device_id`, the device registered under `/admin/stores/{store_id}/devices`

201.description: Issued. The body carries `activation_code`, `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, for the setup sheet. It is returned exactly once, since only its hash is stored, and it is spent the first time a box exchanges it for a credential (ADR-0050)

400.description: tenant_id, store_id or device_id is not a ULID

503.description: The activation store or the entropy source is unavailable

post.summary: A super-admin cancels a device slot's still-issued codes.

requestBody.description: The device slot: `tenant_id`, `store_id` and `device_id`, the device registered under `/admin/stores/{store_id}/devices`

200.description: Every code issued for the slot and not yet spent is cancelled, as for a setup sheet that went astray. The body carries `revoked`, how many were

400.description: tenant_id, store_id or device_id is not a ULID

get.summary:
Lists the console admins — identity and role only, never a credential. Needs
`console.admins.invite` (owner or admin may view the roster).

200.description: Every console administrator, as an array: `id`, `email`, `name`, `role` and `status`. Never a password hash or a TOTP secret

patch.summary:
Changes an admin's role. Needs `console.admins.manage` (owner). Refuses demoting the last active
owner. `404` if there is no admin with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The administrator's id

requestBody.description: `role`: `owner`, `admin`, `ops` or `viewer`

204.description: The role is changed, and audited

400.description: role is not one of the four

404.description: There is no administrator with that id

409.description: The change would demote the last active owner

patch.summary:
Suspends or reactivates an admin. Needs `console.admins.manage` (owner). Refuses suspending the
last active owner. `404` if there is no admin with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The administrator's id

requestBody.description: `status`: `active` or `suspended`

204.description: The status is changed, and audited

400.description: status is not `active` or `suspended`

409.description: The change would suspend the last active owner

get.summary:
A super-admin (any console role) lists the fleet's alerts: the active set by default, or recent
history (active and resolved, newest-seen first, capped) with `?recent=true`.

parameters.name: recent
parameters.description: `true` for recent history, active and resolved, newest-seen first; absent or `false` for the active alerts only

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: With `recent`, the most alerts to return (default 200)

200.description: The alerts, fleet-wide, as an array: each with `id`, `tenant_id` (absent for a server-wide condition), `kind`, `dedup_key`, `severity` (`info`, `warning` or `critical`), `summary`, `detail`, and the Unix-millisecond instants it was first and last seen, acknowledged and resolved

post.summary: A super-admin holding `console.alerts.manage` acknowledges an alert (idempotent).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The alert's id

204.description: Acknowledged, and audited. Idempotent

post.summary:
A super-admin holding `console.alerts.manage` resolves an alert by hand (idempotent — a condition
still firing reopens on the next evaluator tick).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The alert's id

204.description: Resolved, and audited. Idempotent. A condition still present opens again on the evaluator's next pass

get.summary: Lists a tenant's API keys as metadata only — never a secret (super-admin only).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose keys to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's keys, as an array: each with `id`, `store_id` (absent for a tenant-wide key), `scopes`, `revoked` and `expires_at_ms`. Never a token or a secret

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: Provisions a new scoped per-tenant API key and returns the one-time token (super-admin only).
post.description:
Behind the session guard. Mints a CSPRNG id and secret at the edge, [`issue`]s the key, and
persists it (storing only the secret's hash). The token in the `201` body is the only time the
secret is visible.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`; `store_id` to bind the key to one store, or absent for a tenant-wide key (a store's own sync credential must name its store); `scopes`, the only things the key may do: `read_rollups`, `read_config`, `manage_devices`, `place_orders`, `relay_orders` or `publish_events`; and `expires_at_ms`, or absent for a key that never expires

201.description: Provisioned. The body carries the key's `id` and its `token`, `pos_<id>_<secret>`. The token is returned exactly once — only a hash of the secret is stored. The audit entry records the scopes and the expiry, never the token

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID, a scope is unknown, or expires_at_ms is out of range

503.description: The key store or the entropy source is unavailable

delete.summary:
Revokes an API key by id (super-admin only). `204` whether or not a live key was found — revoking
is idempotent, and telling the caller which it was is a needless enumeration signal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The key's id, the ULID half of its token

204.description: No live key has that id any more. Idempotent: the answer is the same whether a live key was found, so it reveals nothing, and only a revocation that retired one is audited

400.description: id is not a ULID

get.summary:
A super-admin lists assignments, by exactly one of four selectors: everyone who works at a store
(`?store_id=` — every assignment that reaches it: its own, its groups' and the tenant's), all a
person holds (`?employee_id=`), those naming a store group (`?store_group_id=`), or those that
reach every store (`?scope_kind=ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT`). Each row says its scope. Behind
[`ConsolePermission::ReadPeople`], the roster's gate: each row names the person it grants
([`Assignment`]).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose assignments to list (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: Everyone who works at this store: every assignment that reaches it, its own, its groups' and the tenant's

parameters.name: employee_id
parameters.description: Everything this person holds

parameters.name: store_group_id
parameters.description: The assignments naming this store group

parameters.name: scope_kind
parameters.description: `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT`: the assignments that reach every store

200.description: The assignments, as an array. Each says its scope and names the person it grants, by name and staff code

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID; not exactly one of store_id, employee_id, store_group_id and scope_kind is sent; the id sent is not a ULID; or scope_kind is not `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT`

post.summary:
A super-admin assigns an employee with a role, at one store, a store group or every store of the
tenant ([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 3; [`requested_scope`] reads which). Audited `assignment.create` with the ids and the
scope ([`assignment_audit`]).
post.description:
Each id is checked before anything is written, because the schema declares no foreign keys
under row-level security and leaves the check to this route (ADR-0070). An employee, store,
group or role the tenant does not have is `404` — another tenant's group included — and one it
has archived is `409` (decision 7): a grant to a retired person, store or group would publish
nobody, and one with a retired role would grant nothing, while the console showed it as a grant.
Each refusal names the field that carried the id. A person who already holds an assignment
there is `409` too ([`already_assigned`]), and nothing is written, audited or published.

An assignment to one store publishes as before, when someone presses publish, and answers `201`
with its id. One to a group or to every store publishes the `permissions` node at once to every
store it reaches — the open stores the group holds, or every open store of the tenant, read
before the write — and answers `201` with its id and each store's outcome (`stores`).

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `employee_id`, `role_template_id`, and where the role is held: a `store_id` for one store, a `store_group_id` for every store the group holds, or `scope_kind` `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT` for every store of the tenant (ADR-0158 decision 3)

201.description: Assigned. The body is `{ "id": … }`. An assignment to a group or to every store is published at once to every open store it reaches, and the body also carries `stores`, each with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`. One to a single store is published when someone publishes

400.description: An id is absent or not a ULID, the scope is named twice or not at all, or scope_kind is not one the route accepts

404.description: The tenant has no such employee, store, store group or role. The error names the field that carried the id

409.description: The employee, store, store group or role is archived, or the person already holds an assignment there. Nothing is written

503.description: The people store, the registry, the store groups or the entropy source is unavailable

delete.summary:
A super-admin removes an assignment — offboarding a person from where it reached. Audited
`assignment.remove` when a row was actually removed, with the ids and the scope it bound; a no-op
removal records nothing.
delete.description:
The removal publishes the `permissions` node at once to every store the assignment reached — its
store, the open stores its group holds, or every open store of the tenant — so the person cannot
sign in there a moment longer
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 7), and answers `200` with each store's outcome.

parameters.name: assignment_id
parameters.description: The assignment's 26-character ULID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: Removed, and every store the assignment reached is published to at once, so the person cannot sign in there a moment longer (ADR-0158 decision 7): `stores` lists each store with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`, which `POST /admin/people/publish` retries

400.description: tenant_id or assignment_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no assignment with that id

503.description: The people store, the registry or the store groups is unreachable

get.summary: A super-admin (any console role) reads the audit trail, filtered by the query string.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: One tenant's entries (a 26-character ULID). Absent, the fleet-wide trail, tenant-global entries included

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: Only entries about this kind of record, such as `store`

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: Only entries about this record

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only entries with this action, such as `store.update`

parameters.name: actor_admin_id
parameters.description: Only entries by this administrator

parameters.name: since_ms
parameters.description: Only entries at or after this instant (Unix ms)

parameters.name: until_ms
parameters.description: Only entries at or before this instant (Unix ms)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Without `offset`, the most recent this many entries (default 200, larger values read as 500). With `offset`, the page size, 1 to 500, refused rather than clamped

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Asks for a page: how many entries to skip, 0 to 100000

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `newest` (the default) or `oldest`. Only with `offset`

200.description: Without `offset`, the newest matching entries as an array; with it, a page: `items`, `total`, `limit` and `offset`. Each entry has `id`, `tenant_id`, the acting administrator's id, email and role, `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `before`, `after`, `request_id` and `at_ms`. An entry about an employee carries the person's staff code only for a role holding console.people.read (ADR-0158 decision 9)

400.description: tenant_id is not a ULID; limit or offset is not an integer in range; or order is sent without offset or is not one the route accepts

get.summary:
A super-admin exports a tenant's catalog items as CSV ([ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md),
Track M5). Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageCatalog`] and audited — the entry records who exported
which domain and how many rows, never the row contents. No price is exported (prices are per-channel
placements, a deferred T2 export); this is the item master only.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: `items.csv`, as a `text/csv` attachment: the header `menu_item_id,name,status,tax_class_id,item_category_id,item_subcategory_id,image_ref`, then one row per item. No price, no translation and no course. A name a spreadsheet would read as a formula is escaped. Audited by row count, never the contents

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

500.description: The CSV could not be built

post.summary:
`POST /admin/catalog/import/items` — the confirm after a dry run: the valid rows are written and
the rejected ones are reported, never written.
post.description:
# Why a row can be applied and reported as applied, and the next one still fail

The rows are separate records and are written one at a time, so this is not a transaction and
does not pretend to be. What it does instead is report per row: a row whose write was refused
comes back as a rejection naming what happened, so re-importing the same file after fixing it is
safe — the rows that already landed are updates at their new version, and the rest are retried.
Wrapping the whole file in one transaction would mean one bad row discarding an operator's whole
afternoon, which is the behaviour the dry run exists to make unnecessary.

An update is conditional on the version read when the import began, so a row somebody else
changed in between is refused rather than silently overwritten
([ADR-0094](../../../docs/adr/0094-optimistic-concurrency-on-admin.md)).

Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageCatalog`] and audited — the row counts, never the contents.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant (a 26-character ULID)

requestBody.description: The CSV `GET /admin/catalog/export/items` writes, with the same header, as the raw request body. A row with a `menu_item_id` this tenant has updates that item; a row with none creates one; any other id is rejected, so a file cannot mint an item id. The format carries no price, translation or course, and an update keeps what it does not carry

200.description: Applied: the valid rows are written one at a time and the report is the dry run's, with any row whose write failed turned into a rejection naming why — `rows`, one per data row in file order, each with its `key` and its `action`: `create`, `update`, or `reject` with a `reason`; and `create_count`, `update_count` and `reject_count`. Not one transaction: re-importing the same file after a fix is safe. An update is conditional on the version read when the import began, so a row changed meanwhile is rejected rather than overwritten. Audited by counts, never the contents

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or the body is not CSV or its header is not the export's

503.description: The catalog store or the entropy source is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /admin/catalog/import/items/dry-run` — what an item-master CSV **would** do, row by row,
writing nothing (roadmap-v3 **F15**, [ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md)).
post.description:
The file is the one `GET /admin/catalog/export/items` writes, which is what makes the pair a
round-trip: export the master, edit it in a spreadsheet, bring it back. It carries no price —
a price is a per-channel placement — so neither the upload nor the report an operator reads can
carry one in clear text.

Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageCatalog`] and not audited, because it changes nothing.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant (a 26-character ULID)

requestBody.description: The CSV `GET /admin/catalog/export/items` writes, with the same header, as the raw request body. A row with a `menu_item_id` this tenant has updates that item; a row with none creates one; any other id is rejected, so a file cannot mint an item id. The format carries no price, translation or course, and an update keeps what it does not carry

200.description: What the file would do, writing nothing: `rows`, one per data row in file order, each with its `key` and its `action`: `create`, `update`, or `reject` with a `reason`; and `create_count`, `update_count` and `reject_count`. like the list.

parameters.name: employee_id
parameters.description: The employee's 26-character ULID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that employs them (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The employee, with an ETag carrying the version it was read at — the token a PATCH must send back as If-Match

400.description: tenant_id or employee_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no employee with that id

patch.summary:
A super-admin renames an employee and/or sets their status. Audited `employee.update` with
before/after id/code/status — never the name.
patch.description:
Archiving the person publishes the `permissions` node at once to every store they are assigned
to, so they cannot sign in at any of them a moment longer
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 7), and the answer is then `200` with each store's outcome. Any other update — a
rename, or restoring an archived person — publishes as before, and answers `204`.

parameters.name: employee_id
parameters.description: The employee's 26-character ULID

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the employee was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, the `name` and the `status` (`active` or `archived`) as they should now stand. The staff code cannot be changed

200.description: Archived. The person is taken off every store they were assigned to at once (ADR-0158 decision 7): `stores` lists each store with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`, which `POST /admin/people/publish` retries. The ETag carries the new version

204.description: Updated: a rename, or restoring an archived person. Nothing is published until someone publishes. The ETag carries the new version

400.description: tenant_id or employee_id is absent or not a ULID, name is blank, status is not `active` or `archived`, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no employee with that id

412.description: The employee changed since you read it: re-read them and try again

503.description: The people store, the registry or the store groups is unreachable

put.summary:
A super-admin sets or resets an employee's PIN. The digits are hashed with Argon2id here and never
returned, stored raw, or **audited** — the entry records only that a PIN was set, by whom
(ADR-0070).
put.description:
A PIN has at least the digits the tenant's `session.pin_min_length` asks for, four where it asks
for none, and at most eight (ADR-0160). This is the one place the minimum is applied: the edge
holds only a PIN's hash. Raising the minimum leaves a PIN already set as it is. If the tenant's
settings cannot be read, the PIN is refused rather than held to four.

parameters.name: employee_id
parameters.description: The employee's 26-character ULID

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and the `pin`: digits only, at least the tenant's `session.pin_min_length` (four where it sets none) and at most eight. The PIN is hashed at once and is never returned, stored in the clear, logged or audited (ADR-0070)

204.description: Set. A store learns the new PIN when its people are next published

400.description: tenant_id or employee_id is absent or not a ULID, or the PIN is not digits of an allowed length

404.description: The tenant has no employee with that id

503.description: The people store, the settings store or the entropy source is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /admin/fees/preview` — a sample bill at one store with rules in place, before they are
written ([ADR-0159](../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md): "the console previews a
sample bill before publishing").
post.description:
A read: it writes nothing and publishes nothing, so it stands behind the fee reads' permission.
It resolves the store's rules with the ones sent in place, compiles them as a publish would, and
assembles the bill with [`crate::fees::sample_bill`], which prices each line and adds it up with
`pos_core`'s own functions, from the store's own published menu, tax table and rounding.

requestBody.description: The tenant, a store, the sales channel (dine-in when absent), the rules as they would be written — each with its scope and scope_id and the rule as a PUT sends it, its fee_id absent for a fee not created yet — and the sample bill's lines, each a menu_item_id from the store's menu and a quantity of 1 to 999. From 1 to 50 lines, and at most 20 rules

200.description: The sample bill as the store would assemble it with those rules in place: each line priced from its menu, each fee charged with its tax and the parts of it taxed at each class, the tax per class, the cash rounding and the total due. Nothing is written or published

400.description: An id is not a ULID, the channel or a scope is not one, a rule is refused as a write would refuse it, or there are no lines, too many lines or rules, or a quantity out of range

404.description: The tenant has no such store, brand or store a rule is for

422.description: The store could not assemble the bill: it has no locale, tax table or menu published (NOT_PUBLISHED), a line is not on its menu for the channel (NOT_ON_MENU), not available (NOT_AVAILABLE) or has no tax rate (TAX_RATE_NOT_CONFIGURED), or a rule it would run cannot apply there

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry, the catalog or the config tree is unreachable

post.summary: `POST /admin/fees/publish` — republishes the fees of one store, or of every store of the tenant.
post.description:
A write republishes every store it reaches by itself. What it cannot see is a change elsewhere
that changes what a store is sent: a store given another brand, or an item added to or taken
out of a category a rule names, which is compiled into items when the fees are published. A
menu publish brings a store's fees along with it; this publishes them without one.

requestBody.description: The tenant, and optionally one store. Without a store, every store of the tenant is republished

200.description: Each store's rules resolved, compiled and republished, with the same per-store outcomes as a write

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no such store

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry or the catalog is unreachable

Invites a new console admin ([ADR-0067](../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md)). Needs

expired token is a generic `401`.

post.summary: Signs a super-admin in: a two-factor login that, on success, sets a host-only session cookie.
post.description:
The session token is minted here — a 256-bit CSPRNG value, at the binary edge — and passed to
[`login`], which stores only its hash ([ADR-0034](../../../docs/adr/0034-super-admin-auth.md)); the
browser gets the token in a `__Host-` cookie. Every credential failure is one generic `401`; a
store outage is a `503`. Described in the console document (`/admin/openapi.json`), not the
integrator one.

requestBody.description: Email, password, and the six-digit TOTP code

204.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set; the body is empty

post.summary: Signs a super-admin out: revokes the session server-side and clears the client cookie.
post.description:
Idempotent — a request with no session, or one the store cannot reach, still clears the client
cookie, so the browser is always logged out even if the server-side row lingers to its TTL.

204.description: Signed out, and idempotent: a request with no session, or one whose store is unreachable, still clears the client cookie

produces is invisible: the cohort looks right on screen, and every batch quietly reports one more

get.summary:
Which devices a store has admitted, which it has retired, and when
([ADR-0118](../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §4).

The read that makes `device.admission.granted` and `device.admission.revoked` a feature rather
than two events with no reader — the state the tree already had one of, and which that record
named as the thing not to repeat. Before this the console's picture of a store's tills was zero
rows, however many tablets the store had actually paired.

**T3**, so `console.data.read` — the same standing the fleet detail beside it takes. The roster
carries device identifiers and instants: no money, and **no employee**, because who admitted a
device is recorded on the store's own disk and reaches no cloud (ADR-0118 §5). The tenant is
named explicitly, as on every `/admin` read, because the console admin is global.

Unwindowed and unpaged: a store's roster is a handful of rows, at the rate it commissions tills.

parameters.description: The store whose roster to read (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.description: The tenant that store belongs to (a 26-character ULID)

Each entry carries the edge-minted local device id, when it was admitted, the paired device whose signed-in manager minted the code (absent for the code a box announces at boot), and when it was retired if it has been. A retired device keeps its row. Empty for a store that has admitted nothing, and for one whose rollup has not been projected yet

post.summary:
Retires one till on a store the console cannot otherwise reach
([ADR-0118](../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §6).
post.description:
**Appends to the `revoked_devices` node, never replaces it**, and the append happens *inside* the
conditional-write retry (see [`publish_config_nodes_with`]). Two admins each retiring a different
till therefore cannot lose each other's entry — which for a deny-list would mean a device left
trading that somebody was told had been retired.

**There is no un-revoke route, and that is the design.** The list is monotone: retiring a device
deletes its pairing row on the box, and no document can put it back. A till that legitimately
returns is a *fresh pairing* with a fresh id, which the list never names.

**A `200` is not proof the device is off.** It means the instruction is published. The store
applies it on its next pull and may refuse it whole — its blast-radius caps are the only place
the roster is authoritative — and it has no channel to say so. Read the admitted-devices roster
to see the retirement land; if it does not, the box's own log says why (ADR-0117).

`console.stores.manage` (Owner/Admin) rather than the `PublishConfig` norm that includes Ops. The
same standing as the lease bump beside it on the Fleet screen, and for the same reason: this is
not a day-to-day publish, it takes a terminal out of service, and a mistake can leave a shop
unable to sell.

The trail records the store and the device id. No employee: who at the console did this is the
audit row's actor, and no *store* employee is involved at all (ADR-0118 §5).

parameters.description: The store the till belongs to (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The deny-list now names the device, as of the config version returned. The store carries it out on its next config pull — within thirty seconds for a store with a working link, and on its next boot otherwise — and the admitted-devices roster then shows the device retired. Re-revoking a device already on the list succeeds and adds nothing

where a store's data may rest, which is the same judgement the bump that put it there was, and
the person who makes it is the person who moves stores between machines.

# It answers one difference, not the store

The request names both country codes and the write refuses `FailedPrecondition` when either has
moved since the console drew the screen. Without that check an admin could acknowledge a
difference that no longer exists — or worse, one that changed to something they never saw — and
the record would say a person approved a transfer they were never shown. The row then keeps the
pair, so the *read* applies the same rule for free: an answer stops standing when the store
moves, and the warning comes back unanswered.

Refused for a store with no difference at all, because there is nothing to answer: a store whose
region agrees, or which has no region, or which has published no country, would otherwise
accumulate reasons for questions nobody asked.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Two-factor sign-in, the session it issues, and the second-factor levers (ADR-0034, ADR-0060); an administrator's own sessions, listed and revoked; and who administers the console, by invitation, role and status (ADR-0067). An invitation's token and an enrolment's TOTP secret are each returned once and stored only as a hash or not at all. The last active owner cannot be demoted or suspended. Everything else on this surface stands behind the session these routes establish.

tags.name: config releases
tags.description: A release is one decision and many writes (ADR-0125): a named set of config publishes, aimed at a cohort or an explicit store list, timed once — in each store's own clock or at a single instant. Scheduling one expands it to a `scheduled_publishes` row per (node, store) pair, which ADR-0077's activator applies. These routes write no config versions of their own.

tags.name: store groups
tags.description: The cohorts a tenant publishes to as one, and their membership (ADR-0122). A group holds no configuration: publishing to one calls the same per-store publish once per member, so the config tree's four layers and the store's sync path are untouched. Membership is replaced wholesale under the group's own ETag, because a cohort is a set and a delta API merges two admins' concurrent edits into one neither of them chose.

tags.name: integrator access
tags.description: The credentials and destinations of the `/v1` integrator surface: a tenant's scoped API keys (ADR-0037) and the webhook endpoints a store's events are sent to (ADR-0032). A key's token and an endpoint's signing secret are each returned once, when it is made; no read returns either. A webhook URL is checked before it is stored, so it can never point into the cloud's own network. Revoking a key and deleting an endpoint are idempotent and say nothing about whether one existed.

tags.name: integrations
tags.description: The vendors this cloud can talk to, and what each needs (ADR-0153). Documented because it is the contract a fork's own console draws its connection forms from: the form is the provider's settings schema, so a console that hard-coded one vendor's fields would be wrong the day a second is added.

tags.name: reason codes
tags.description: The managed list a void, a discount, a comp, a refund, a drawer opening, a staff rejection, either cash movement and either stock correction must cite (ADR-0115, `docs/pos-spec.md` §11 item 2). Documented rather than deferred because it is a **fraud control**: a fork writing its own console needs to know that ids are server-minted, that an entry leaves service by going inactive rather than by being deleted, and that every write is conditional.

tags.name: devices
tags.description: What a store has actually admitted (ADR-0118). Documented rather than deferred with the rest of the device surface because it is the **only** read that answers it: a store admits tablets locally and offline, and until these events the cloud's picture of a store's tills was zero rows. Note the two identity spaces — the ids here are minted by the edge at pairing, and nothing joins them to the console-minted ids of `/admin/stores/{store_id}/devices`.

tags.name: box activation
tags.description: The device slots a store has, and how a box earns the credential for one (ADR-0050, ADR-0065, ADR-0148). An administrator registers a slot, then either issues a one-time activation code for its setup sheet or binds the code a box with no store shows on its screen. Either way the box receives its credential once, and only a hash of it is kept. An activation code is returned exactly once and can be cancelled until it is spent.

tags.name: device onboarding
tags.description: How a store's printers, kitchen displays and tills come into service (ADR-0041, ADR-0100, ADR-0112). A store proposes each device it discovers; an administrator approves it, stating how it is attached and which station it serves, or rejects it. A till is never discovered, so an administrator creates it directly. Nothing reaches a store until its approved devices are published as its `devices` node.

tags.name: printers
tags.description: What paper each approved printer takes and whether it cuts it (ADR-0160 decision 2), which printer a till's receipts go to and the languages they print in (decision 4), and the float a till's drawer opens with (ADR-0167 decision 4), the terminal whose print agent drives a printer (ADR-0112), and whether a cash drawer is wired to it (ADR-0165). A fork's own console needs to know that a printer nobody has set prints as 80 mm paper with a cutter, that a till nobody has set prints and opens its drawer as the store does, and that nothing reaches a store until its devices are published.

tags.name: catalog items
tags.description: A tenant's item master (ADR-0066, ADR-0075): each item's name and per-locale names, tax class, categories, course and photo. An item carries no price; a price belongs to its placement on a menu. Item ids are minted by the server and are what an order names an item by. The master round-trips as a CSV: export it, edit it in a spreadsheet, check the file with a dry run, then apply it. A file can update or create items but never mint an id. Nothing reaches a store until its catalog is published.

tags.name: catalog taxonomy
tags.description: How a tenant's catalog is sorted (ADR-0066, ADR-0130): item categories and their sub-categories, which reporting groups an item under; display categories and their sub-categories, which a till's layout shows; and courses, the order a table's dishes are served in. Ids are minted by the server, records are archived rather than deleted, and every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. An item category or sub-category that active items still use cannot be archived. Nothing reaches a store until its catalog is published.

tags.name: countries
tags.description: The read-only master data a console picks a store's country and locale from (ADR-0074, ADR-0105): the country modules this build carries, with the currency, number format, retention and till facts each fixes, and the content locales the platform serves. Fixed when the server starts.

tags.name: campaigns
tags.description: The promotions a tenant authors for its stores' pricing engine (ADR-0077): item, combo, bill, voucher and manual campaigns, and the codes a voucher campaign redeems. Ids are minted by the server and every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. Nothing reaches a store until its campaigns are published. A voucher code carries redeemable value, so even listing codes needs `console.campaigns.manage`, and no audit entry records a code or a discount's terms.

tags.name: reports
tags.description: What a store did over a window of its trading days, read from the materialised rollup and never from the event log (ADR-0036, ADR-0081): its activity counts, its takings, fees by code (ADR-0159) and tax by component (ADR-0168), each as a read or a CSV download, and the X or Z report for one day. Prices are T2, so every read or export of an amount needs `console.reports.revenue`; the activity counts need only `console.data.read`. An export is audited by how many rows it held, never what they held. Resetting a store's rollup has the projector rebuild it from the event log.

tags.name: fleet
tags.description: Where each store runs and how it is standing (ADR-0068, ADR-0110, ADR-0114): its last contact and whether it is online, the configuration and binary it runs, what it holds unsent, and whether the country its data rests in agrees with the one it is registered in. Online and current are derived when read, never stored. The one write answers a region difference, the compliance warning the single-store read shows.

tags.name: operations
tags.description: Whether the cloud and the fleet are working (ADR-0068, ADR-0073, ADR-0078): the alerts the evaluator keeps, fleet-wide, with their acknowledgement and resolution; the health of each background loop; and the reconciliation runs that show no store's events were lost.

tags.name: registry
tags.description: The organisation a console administers (ADR-0065): its tenants, the brands a tenant trades under, and its stores. Every record is created active with an id minted by the server and leaves service by being archived rather than deleted; every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. A new tenant is given its six starting roles (ADR-0158). A store's devices, configuration and reports are separate surfaces under the store's path.

tags.name: subject requests
tags.description: The instrument the Data Protection contact uses to carry out one data subject's access, portability or erasure request under Vietnam's PDPD (Decree 13/2023) or the GDPR (ADR-0076). It assists that process and records it; it does not decide it. Before any of these routes is used, a person confirms the lawful basis and the subject's identity, and confirms consent, retention and, for customer analytics, a DPIA. A request from an EU resident is escalated to the Data Protection contact rather than actioned here, and moving an export across a border needs a DTA or explicit consent first. Each route acts on one subject of one tenant: there is no list, no bulk export and no cross-tenant read, because a bulk export is an escalation, not a feature. Only an owner holds `console.subjects.manage`, and every call is audited with ids and counts, never a personal value.

tags.name: audit
tags.description: Every console write, who made it and when (ADR-0069), read by any console role. An entry records ids, codes and statuses, never a person's name or a secret; an employee's staff code is shown only to a role that may read the roster (ADR-0158 decision 9).

tags.name: settings
tags.description: Every value a store may run differently (ADR-0160, `docs/configuration.md`). A value is written once, at the tenant, a brand, a store group or one store; each store runs the most specific value that reaches it, and every store a write reaches is republished in the same request. Documented because a fork's own console draws its settings screen from the catalogue here.

tags.name: people
tags.description: Who may do what at a store (ADR-0070, ADR-0158): the people a tenant employs, the roles that say what each may do, the assignments that give a person a role at one store, a store group or every store, and the publish that compiles them into a store's `permissions` node. Staff records name people, so reading them needs `console.people.read`; the permission catalogue and the roles name nobody. A write is audited with ids, codes and statuses, never a name or a PIN. Archiving a person or a role, removing an assignment, and assigning to a group or every store publish to every store the change reaches before they answer, and report each store's outcome. The readiness read names roles and counts people, and names no person.

tags.name: fees
tags.description: The charges a bill adds — a service charge, a packaging fee, a delivery fee (ADR-0159). A rule is written once, at the tenant, a brand or one store; for each fee a store runs the most specific rule that reaches it, and every store a write reaches is republished in the same request. An item list may name item categories, which are compiled into items when the store is published. Documented because a fork's own console draws its fee screen from these routes, and needs to know that a store which cannot apply a rule is left as it is rather than sent part of its list.

tags.name: config
tags.description: A store's published configuration (ADR-0033). The authoring routes are still coverage debt; the per-node read here is documented because it is what a fork's own console needs to answer the operator's actual question — which node is stale — and because it carries no configuration values at all, only which nodes exist and when each was last published.
